Speaker's Card/Request to Speak: If you would like to address the City Council on a scheduled agenda item, including a Consent Calendar item, a Regular Council Business item, a Public Hearing item, or Public Comments, please complete the "Request to Speak Form." The card is at the table at the entrance to the City Council Chamber. Please identify on the card your name and the item on which you would like to speak and return to the City Clerk. The "Request to Speak Form" assists the Mayor in ensuring that all persons wishing to address the City Council are recognized. It also ensures the accurate identification of meeting participants in the City Council minutes. Your name will be called at the time the matter is heard by the City Council. City policy is to limit public testimony to up to three minutes per speaker depending on relevant circumstances (unless the time limit is extended by the Mayor), which includes the presentation of electronic or audio visual information. Speakers may not yield their time to other persons.
Please take notice that the order of scheduled agenda items below and/or the time they are actually heard, considered and decided may be modified by the Mayor or the City Council during the course of the meeting, so please stay alert.

NOTICE TO THE PUBLIC
LIVE BROADCASTING AND REBROADCASTING
Regular City Council meetings are broadcast live every 2nd and 4th Tuesday of the month at 4 p.m. and are replayed on Tuesdays at 4 p.m. (in weeks in which there is not a live City Council meeting), Sundays at 11 a.m., Wednesdays at 7 p.m., and Thursdays at 10 a.m. until the next City Council meeting. All broadcasts can be viewed on Cox Communications Local Access Channel 30 and U-Verse Channel 99. City Council meetings are also available via live webcast and at any time for replaying through the City's ICTV webpage at cityofirvine.org/ictv . For more information, please contact the City Clerk''s office at (949) 724-6205.
ADJOURNMENT
At 11:00 p.m., the City Council will determine which of the remaining agenda items can be considered and acted upon prior to 12:00 midnight and will continue all other items on which additional time is required until a future City Council meeting. All meetings are scheduled to terminate at 12:00 midnight.
STAFF REPORTS
As a general rule, staff reports or other written documentation have been prepared or organized with respect to each item of business listed on the agenda. Copies of these materials are on file with the City Clerk and are available for public inspection and copying once the agenda is publicly posted, (at least 72 hours prior to a regular City Council meeting). Staff reports can also be downloaded from the City's website at cityofirvine.org beginning the Friday prior to the scheduled City Council meeting on Tuesday.
In addition, meetings can be viewed live at the time posted on the agenda and related staff reports can be opened and viewed simultaneously along with the streaming of the meeting. To view the meeting, go to cityofirvine.org/ictv .
If you have any questions regarding any item of business on the agenda for this meeting, or any of the staff reports or other documentation relating to any agenda item, please contact City Clerk staff at (949)724-6205.
SUPPLEMENTAL MATERIAL RECEIVED AFTER THE POSTING OF THE AGENDA
Any supplemental writings or documents distributed to a majority of the City Council regarding any item on this agenda after the posting of the agenda will be available for public review in the City Clerk''s Office, One Civic Center Plaza, Irvine, California, during normal business hours. In addition, such writings or documents will be made available for public review at the respective public meeting.
If you have any questions regarding any item of business on the agenda for this meeting, or any of the staff reports or other documentation relating to any agenda item, please contact City Clerk staff at (949)724-6205.
SUBMITTAL OF INFORMATION BY MEMBERS OF THE PUBLIC FOR DISSEMINATION OR PRESENTATION AT PUBLIC MEETINGS
Media Types and Guidelines
1. Written Materials/Handouts:
Any member of the public who desires to submit documentation in hard copy form may do so prior to the meeting or at the time he/she addresses the City Council. Please provide 15 copies of the information to be submitted and file with the City Clerk at the time of arrival to the meeting. This information will be disseminated to the City Council at the time testimony is given.
2. Large Displays/Maps/Renderings:
Any member of the public who desires to display freestanding large displays or renderings in conjunction with their public testimony is asked to notify the City Clerk's Office at (949)724-6205 no later than 12:00 noon on the day of the scheduled meeting so that an easel can be made available, if necessary.
3. Electronic Documents/Audio-Visuals:
Any member of the public who desires to display information electronically in conjunction with their public testimony is asked to submit the information to the Public Information Office (PIO) no later than 12:00 noon on the day of the scheduled meeting. To facilitate your request contact the PIO Office at (949)724-6253 or the City Clerk''s Office at (949)724-6205.
Information must be provided on CD, DVD, or VHS; or, emailed by 12:00 noon on the day of the scheduled meeting to pio@ci.irvine.ca.us . Members of the public will be asked to provide their name, identify the meeting and the agenda item to be addressed, and a day time phone number.
The PIO office will notify the person submitting the information as soon as possible prior to the meeting if the information cannot be accessed or if the version provided is incompatible with the City''s system. Every effort will be made by City staff to facilitate the presentation.
CITY SERVICES TO FACILITATE ACCESS TO PUBLIC MEETINGS
It is the intention of the City of Irvine to comply with the Americans With Disabilities Act (ADA) in all respects. If, as an attendee or a participant at this meeting, you will need special assistance beyond what is normally provided, the City of Irvine will attempt to accommodate you in every reasonable manner. Please contact the City Clerk's Office at (949)724-6205.
Assisted listening devices are available at the meeting for individuals with hearing impairments. Notification 48 hours prior to the meeting will enable the City to make reasonable arrangements to ensure accessibility to this meeting. (28 CFR 35. 102-35. 104 ADA Title II)
CHALLENGING CITY DECISIONS
The time limit within which to commence any lawsuit or legal challenge to any quasi-adjudicative decision made by the City is governed by Section 1094.6 of the Code of Civil Procedure, unless a shorter limitations period is specified by any other provision. Under Section 1094.6, any lawsuit or legal challenge to any quasi-adjudicative decision made by the City must be filed no later than the 90th day following the date on which such decision becomes final. Any lawsuit or legal challenge that is not filed within this 90-day period will be barred.
If a person wishes to challenge the nature of the above actions in court, they may be limited to raising only those issues they or someone else raised at the meeting described in this notice, or in written correspondence delivered to the City of Irvine, at or prior to the meeting. In addition, judicial challenge may be limited or barred where the interested party has not sought and exhausted all available administrative remedies.
COMMUNICATION AND ELECTRONIC DEVICES
To minimize distractions, please be sure all personal communication and electronic devices are turned off or on silent mode.
MEETING SCHEDULE
Regular meetings of the City Council are held on the second and fourth Tuesdays of each month at 4:00 p.m. Study Sessions and/or Closed Sessions are periodically held prior to the start of the regular meeting. Agendas are available at the following locations:
 City Clerk's Office
 Police Department
 Front Entrance of City Hall
 University Park Center (Culver/Michelson)
 Walnut Village Center (Culver/Walnut)
 Northwood Town Center (Irvine Blvd./Yale)
 City's web page at www.ci.irvine.ca.us

MINUTES

  CITY COUNCIL
  REGULAR MEETING

  March 14, 2017
  City Council Chamber
  One Civic Center Plaza
  Irvine, CA 92606

CALL TO ORDER

The regular meeting of the Irvine City Council was called to order at 4:10 p.m. on
February 28, 2017 in the City Council Chamber, Irvine Civic Center, One Civic Center
Plaza, Irvine, California; Mayor Wagner presiding.

ROLL CALL

  Present:  5  Councilmember:  Melissa Fox
  Councilmember:  Jeffrey Lalloway
  Councilmember:  Christina Shea
  Mayor Pro Tempore:  Lynn Schott*
  Mayor:  Donald P. Wagner

  * Mayor Pro Tempore Schott arrived at 4:13 p.m.

1.  SCOPING SESSION

  1.1  SCOPING SESSION FOR A GENERAL PLAN AMENDMENT REQUEST
  REPRESENTING AN EXCHANGE OF NON-RESIDENTIAL BUILDING
  SQUARE FOOTAGE FOR NEW RESIDENTIAL UNITS WITHIN
  PLANNING AREA 12 (OAK CREEK) AND PLANNING AREA 40
  (CYPRESS VILLAGE)
 City Council Minutes  March 14, 2017

  Joel Belding, Principal Planner, presented the staff report and responded
  to questions. Tim Gehrich, Deputy Director of Community Development,
  and Stephanie Frady, Senior Planner, were also available for questions.

  The following individuals spoke in support of delaying and/or discontinuing
  the application process:

  Steve Parker
  Rebecca Ward, Irvine resident
  Claudia Sawaya
  Harvey Liss, Irvine resident
  Mark Newgent, Irvine resident

  Courtney Santos, Irvine resident, spoke in support of moving forward with
  processing the subject application.

  Mike Leblanc, representing the Irvine Company, provided a brief overview
  of the projects and responded to questions related to affordable housing,
  traffic, child care and schools.

  City Council discussion included: traffic impacts surrounding the projects
  and how those concerns could be mitigated; density of the proposed
  projects in comparison to similar projects in the Irvine Spectrum; noted
  upcoming review of the General Plan update; questioned the number of
  similar projects under review; expressed concern about the overcrowding
  of nearby schools and capacity for those living within assigned
  boundaries; questioned provisions related to the recent school bond
  measure (Measure E) and expressed concerns about the impacts on
  taxpayers; questioned the number of affordable housing units and why the
  Irvine Company was not utilizing other apartment communities within its
  portfolio for mid-range affordable housing; expressed a desire to hold a
  workshop for the purpose of a more global discussion specific to
  affordable housing and existing inventory; noted that the projects would be
  further analyzed during the application review process by the Planning
  and Transportation Commissions prior to returning to the City Council for
  final review; noted the City Council’s ability to deny the application in the
  future; and reiterated the tentative timeline for Commission and City
  Council review.

  ACTION:  Moved by Councilmember Lalloway, seconded by
  Councilmember Schott, to:

  Direct staff to process the subject application.

  Prepared by the City Clerk’s Office  2
 City Council Minutes  March 14, 2017

  The motion carried as follows:

  AYES:  3  COUNCILMEMBERS:  Lalloway,  Schott  and
  Wagner

  NOES:  2  COUNCILMEMBERS:  Fox and Shea

  ABSENT: 0  COUNCILMEMBERS:  None

  2.  CLOSED SESSION

  2.1  CONFERENCE WITH LEGAL COUNSEL – ANTICIPATED LITIGATION:

  a. Potential initiation of litigation pursuant to paragraph (4) of
  subdivision (d) of Section 54956.9: 1 potential case

  b. Significant exposure to litigation pursuant to paragraph (2) or (3) of
  subdivision (d) of Section 54956.1: 1 potential case

  City Attorney Melching announced that Closed Session Item No. 2.1a was
  related to the Southern California Edison Safari Substation (Substation)
  matter; and noted that Item No. 2.1b would be removed from the agenda.

  The following individuals spoke in opposition to any discussion related to
  land use matters with respect to the proposed Substation and in support of
  discussing such matters in open session:

  Mike Aguirre
  Daniel Kim
  William Klassen
  Doug Bender
  Norman Voo

  City Council discussion included: questioning parameters of Closed
  Session matters with respect to the Brown Act; and public noticing
  requirements, including the reporting of action taken in Closed Session.

  Jeff Melching, City Attorney, reiterated the removal of Closed Session
  Item No. 2.1b due to a scrivener’s error; and provided a brief summary
  related to the criteria for listing Closed Session items with respect to the
  Safe Harbor Provisions in the Government Code.

  RECESS

  Mayor Wagner convened the City Council meeting to Closed Session at 5:30 p.m.

  Prepared by the City Clerk’s Office  3
 City Council Minutes  March 14, 2017

  RECONVENE TO THE CITY COUNCIL MEETING

  Mayor Wagner reconvened the regular City Council meeting at 6:40 p.m. City Attorney
  Melching, on behalf of the City Council, announced that with respect to Closed Session
  Item No. 2.1a, by a 3-2 vote (Mayor Wagner and Councilmember Shea dissenting), the
  City Council directed that the City of Irvine initiate a proceeding with the California
  Public Utilities Commission concerning the Safari Substation matter, pursuant to
  General Order 131(d) of the Public Utilities Code.

  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  Mayor Wagner led the Pledge of Allegiance.

  INVOCATION

  Mayor Wagner invited Pastor Frank Winans from Woodbridge Community Church in
  Irvine to provide the invocation.

  3.  PRESENTATIONS

  3.1  Proclaim March as “National Nutrition Month”

  Mayor Wagner introduced individuals from the California Academy of
  Nutrition and Dietetics – Orange District and presented a proclamation in
  recognition of “National Nutrition Month.”

  3.2  Employee Recognition - 25 and 30 Years of Service

  City Manager Joyce recognized the following individuals for their years of
  service and presented each with a Certificate of Recognition:

  •  Kelly Feldman, Community Services Supervisor, 25 years
  •  John Condon, Area Lieutenant – Crossroads, 30 years
  •  Dan Jung, Special Assistant to the Chief of Police, 30 years

  CITY MANAGER'S REPORT

  There was no report.

  Prepared by the City Clerk’s Office  4
 City Council Minutes  March 14, 2017

  ANNOUNCEMENTS/COMMITTEE REPORTS/COUNCIL REPORTS

  Mayor Pro Tempore Schott made the following announcements:

  •  On Sunday, February 26, the City of Irvine held a groundbreaking ceremony
  for the Northwood Gratitude and Honor Memorial Expansion project. The
  event was held in partnership with the Northwood Memorial Committee, and
  provided the community an opportunity to learn more about the memorial
  and the expansion. The public is invited to attend the Northwood Memorial
  Candle Lighting Ceremony on Sunday, May 28 to see the completed
  expansion. For information, visit cityofirvine.org/specialevents.

  •  Irvine and Orange County residents are invited to the last two community
  meetings as part of the City’s public outreach regarding the Orange County
  Great Park. The first will be held at 6:30 p.m. on Monday, March 27 at the
  Honda Center in Anaheim; and the second will be held at 10 a.m. on
  Sunday, April 2 at the South Cost Chinese Cultural Center in Irvine, which
  will also be held in Mandarin. No RSVP is required. For information, visit
  cityofirvine.org.

  Mayor Wagner made the following announcements:

  •  On Thursday, March 9, the Irvine Animal Cere Center welcomed the
  10,000th animal, a dog named Gunner, through its Third Chance for Pets
  program. Started in 1999, the program brings in animals from overcrowded
  or underfunded shelters in California to the Center, where they have a better
  chance of being adopted. The 10,000th pet was a two-year-old Siberian
  husky from Animal Friends of the Valleys, a rescue organization in
  Wildomar, and was recently adopted. The Third Chance for Pets program is
  managed by City staff and primarily supported through donations. For
  information, visit cityofirvine.org/animals or call 949-724-7740.

  •  The Orange County Great Park is hosting a photography exhibit, featuring
  the work of veteran surf photographer Tom Carey, through April 23. The
  exhibit in the Great Park Gallery, “Surfing with Tom Carey,” features
  imagery of some of the world’s finest surfers at iconic beaches. The exhibit
  is open from noon to 4 p.m. Thursdays and Fridays, and 10 a.m. to 4 p.m.
  Saturdays and Sundays. For information, visit ocgp.org.

  ADDITIONS AND DELETIONS

  There were no additions or deletions to the agenda.

  This item was agendized at the request of Councilmember Fox, who
  asked for City Council support to direct staff to coordinate a community
  meeting in collaboration with other stakeholders and faith-based
  communities to reassure every segment of our community that the City of
  Irvine stands to serve all with fairness, compassion and understanding.

  The following individuals spoke in support of hosting a community
  meeting:

  Courtney Santos, Irvine resident
  Lauren Johnson
  Asmaa Ahmed
  Robin Gourier

  The following individuals spoke in opposition:

  John Jaeger, Irvine resident
  Steve Greenberg, Irvine resident

  Bryan Fazio, Irvine resident, submitted a Request to Speak card but did
  not speak.

  City Council discussion included: the recent threat made against the
  Jewish Community Center and similar facilities across the nation; noted
  recent situations of intolerance experienced by some community
  members; reaffirming the City’s commitment to diversity and civil rights;
  noted Orange County Supervisor Todd’s Spitzer’s support and
  commitment to participate; questioned the process for coordinating this
  type of community meeting, including attendees and the public noticing
  process; expressed concern that this issue expands beyond Irvine;
  whether Irvine has experienced an increase in hate crimes; suggested
  agendizing the matter at an upcoming City Council meeting; partnering
  with religious institutions and other agencies; Brown Act requirements and

  Prepared by the City Clerk’s Office  13

  other meeting logistical issues; and questioned how to accomplish the
  intended goal.

  Mike Hamel, Director of Public Safety/Chief of Police, responded to
  questions related to hate crimes.

  ACTION:  Moved by Councilmember Fox to:

  Organize a community meeting, possibly in cooperation with other
  stakeholders, such as the Orange County Human Relations
  Commission or members of our faith based community, with the

  that the City of Irvine stands to serve all with fairness, compassion
  and understanding to the extent that meeting would need to be

  Following the motion, Mayor Wagner suggested working with staff to

  crimes very seriously, as well as educating the community on resources
  available at City Hall and throughout the City.
